---
emoji: "🆕"
name: "Weekly What's New"
description: Opens a PR to update the What's New page
private: true

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
  schedule:
    - cron: weekly on sunday around 9am

if: github.repository == 'MicrosoftDocs/architecture-center-pr'

permissions:
  contents: read
  issues: read
  pull-requests: read
  copilot-requests: write

model: sonnet
engine:
  id: copilot
  copilot-sdk: true
max-tool-denials: 3
strict: true

sandbox:
  agent:
    sudo: false

tracker-id: generate-whats-new

network:
  allowed:
    - defaults
    - github

safe-outputs:
  create-pull-request:
    expires: 6d
    draft: false
    protected-files: blocked
    reviewers: [ckittel]
    assignees: [ckittel]
    max: 1
    if-no-changes: warn
    allowed-files:
      - docs/changelog.md
      - docs/feed.atom
    max-patch-files: 2
    signed-commits: true

tools:
  cli-proxy: true
  github:
    mode: gh-proxy
    toolsets: [default]
  edit:
  bash: true
  cache-memory:
    retention-days: 90
    allowed-extensions: [".json"]

timeout-minutes: 20
---

# Update AAC's "What's New" page

Review the pull requests merged into `main` in the last 30 days and open a PR that updates the existing "What's New" page (`docs/changelog.md`) and its companion RSS feed (`docs/feed.atom`) with the articles that meaningfully changed. You look back 30 days and run about weekly, so most pull requests in the window were already handled in a prior run; the procedure below tells you how to skip those and log only what's new.

You're the sole generator of these two files. No other script maintains them, so keep the autogenerated notice in `docs/changelog.md` intact.

## Procedure

1. Load the exclusion ledger described in [The exclusion ledger](#the-exclusion-ledger).
2. List the pull requests merged into `main` in the last 30 days.
   - Fetch every pull request in the window, not just the first page. List APIs and `gh pr list` might not contain all results, so paginate through all results or approach with high limits.
3. Decide what to do with each pull request:
   - If its PR number is already in the ledger, skip it. You already evaluated it and excluded it.
   - Otherwise, if its merge commit SHA already appears in `docs/changelog.md`, skip it. It's already logged.
   - Otherwise, evaluate it and classify it as described in [Classifying changes](#classifying-changes). Either log it, or exclude it as minor or renamed.
4. For every pull request you're logging, add or update its entries in `docs/changelog.md` and `docs/feed.atom` as described in [Writing the entries](#writing-the-entries).
5. Trim the page to its rolling window as described in [Rolling window](#rolling-window).
6. Update the ledger: add an entry for each pull request you newly excluded this run, prune entries older than 40 days, and write it back. Do this even if you log nothing, so the exclusions persist.
7. Finish:
   - If you logged at least one article, set the `ms.date` front matter in `docs/changelog.md` to today's date and open the PR.
   - If nothing qualifies, don't open a PR. Call the `noop` tool with a message that explains why: `{"noop": {"message": "No action needed: [brief explanation]"}}`.

## Classifying changes

- Exclude a pull request as **minor** when its changes are any combination of the following, and nothing else:
  - An article was only touched because of URL updates (an article it links to moved to a new URL).
  - An article only had metadata changed.
  - An article only had a couple of lines changed, such as an added point or a typo fix.

- Treat a renamed article as an existing article, never as new. A rename on its own, including a `.yml` -> `.md` conversion (or the reverse) or a simple file rename, doesn't make an article new.

  Exclude a pull request as **renamed** only when its sole non-minor change is effectively the rename itself. If the same pull request also makes substantive changes to the article, don't exclude it.

- Log everything else as a change.

## Writing the entries

- Use the style of the current page to guide how you add new entries or update existing ones.

- Order months in reverse chronological order, newest first. The most recent month is always the topmost `##` section on the page. When a new month begins, add its section above the previous month's section, never below it. Within each month, keep the `### New articles` subsection before the `### Updated articles` subsection.

- Use the "Sentence case" version of each article's title, not the "Book Title" case.

- When you link to a commit, link to the `architecture-center` mirror, not the `architecture-center-pr` repo. Both repos share the same commit SHAs, so reuse the same SHA in the mirror URL.

- When an article received more than one significant pull request, log each one in the month it merged. Keep a separate change link for every significant PR, even if that means one entry shows two change links in the same month, or the same article appears under more than one month. Each PR's SHA is tracked independently, so a later significant PR to an already-logged article still counts as new.

- In `docs/feed.atom`, use each article's `description` front matter as the entry's `<summary>`.

- Give each `docs/feed.atom` entry a globally unique, stable `<id>`. An Atom `<id>` identifies the entry, not the destination page, so two entries must never share an `<id>`, even when they point at the same article. When you add an entry for an article that already has an entry in the feed (for example, a later update to a previously logged article), don't reuse the plain page URL as the `<id>`. Append that change's commit SHA to the page URL as a fragment to keep the `<id>` unique and stable, for example `https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/architecture/patterns/choreography#ec74a8d712`. Keep the `<link href>` as the plain page URL. Before you finish, confirm every `<id>` in the feed is unique.

- Validate the feed's XML syntax. For example, run `xmllint --noout docs/feed.atom`. Fix any issues that were introduced.

- Only change `ms.date` when you're already making content changes to the page. Never bump `ms.date` on its own, because a date change alone must not trigger a PR.

## Rolling window

The page keeps a rolling history of the four most recent months, ordered newest first. When a new month begins, add its section at the top of the page (above the previously newest month) and remove the oldest month that rolls off the bottom, along with its RSS feed entries.

## The exclusion ledger

The ledger is a deduplication cache. It exists so you don't re-evaluate pull requests you already decided to exclude as minor or renamed. Those exclusion decisions leave no trace in `docs/changelog.md`, so without the ledger you'd re-evaluate them every week.

`docs/changelog.md` on `main`, not the ledger, is the source of truth for what's already logged. A pull request counts as logged only when its merge commit SHA appears in `docs/changelog.md`. This is what makes the workflow self-healing: if an earlier run opened a changelog PR that was never merged, was closed, or was reverted, the SHA is absent from `main`, so you log the article again. Never record a `logged` decision in the ledger; it holds exclusions only.

- The ledger is a single JSON file at `/tmp/gh-aw/cache-memory/whats-new-processed.json`, persisted across runs through cache memory.

- Load it at the start of every run. Treat a missing or empty file as an empty ledger (`[]`), not an error. This condition happens on the first run and whenever the cache expires. An empty ledger is harmless: it only means you re-evaluate the pull requests in the window and reach the same conclusions.

- Each entry records one pull request you evaluated and deliberately excluded: its PR number, its merge commit SHA, the exclusion reason (`skipped-minor` or `renamed`), and the date you evaluated it. For example: `{"pr": 1234, "sha": "abc123", "decision": "skipped-minor", "evaluated": "2026-08-02"}`.

- Prune entries whose `evaluated` date is more than 40 days ago before writing the ledger back. The ledger only needs to cover the 30-day lookback window, and pruning keeps the file small.
